questions.prompt: A query that used to be fast is now slow in production. How do you diagnose it?
questions.zh: 一条以前很快的查询现在在线上变慢了。你怎么诊断？
outline: Find it in the slow query log or database monitoring, with real parameters
Read the execution plan: scans, join order, estimated versus actual rows
Ask what changed: data volume, stale statistics, a new code path
Fix options: add or adjust an index, rewrite the query, refresh statistics
Verify on production-like data, then watch it after release

chunks.zh: （优化器）放着索引不用，也就是“索引失效”

followUps: Why might the optimizer choose a full scan even though an index exists?
How do you add an index to a huge table safely?

questions.prompt: How do you decide which indexes to create, and what's the cost of having too many?
questions.zh: 该建哪些索引，你是怎么决定的？索引建得太多有什么代价？
outline: Start from real query patterns: filters, joins, sort order
Composite index column order: equality columns first, then range or sort
A covering index answers the query without going back to the table
A low-selectivity column on its own rarely helps
Every index slows writes and takes space; drop the unused ones

chunks.zh: （索引或过滤条件的）选择性、区分度

followUps: How do you find indexes that nobody uses?

questions.prompt: Explain the practical differences between transaction isolation levels. Which anomalies have actually bitten you?
questions.zh: 讲讲各个事务隔离级别在实际使用中的区别。哪些异常现象真的坑过你？
outline: Read committed: no dirty reads, but non-repeatable reads are possible
Repeatable read or snapshot: a stable view, but write skew can remain
Serializable: safest, at the price of more aborts or blocking
Defaults differ: PostgreSQL uses read committed, MySQL InnoDB repeatable read
Real bugs: lost updates and check-then-act races; fix with locks or constraints

chunks.zh: 串行化（最严格的隔离级别）

followUps: Why don't most systems simply run everything at serializable?

questions.prompt: Two users edit the same record at the same time. How do you stop one from silently overwriting the other?
questions.zh: 两个用户同时编辑同一条记录。你怎么防止其中一个悄悄覆盖掉另一个的修改？
outline: Name the problem: a lost update
Optimistic: version column, update only if the version matches, else report conflict
Pessimistic: select for update holds a row lock for the transaction
Optimistic suits rare conflicts; pessimistic suits heavy contention and short transactions
For human edits, show the conflict instead of retrying blindly
followUps: How would you handle this if the edit takes the user ten minutes?

questions.prompt: How do you choose between a relational database and a NoSQL store for a new system?
questions.zh: 一个新系统该用关系型数据库还是 NoSQL，你怎么选？
outline: Start from access patterns, consistency needs, and expected scale
Relational: flexible queries, joins, transactions; a safe default
Document or key-value: simple lookups, flexible schema, easier horizontal scaling
NoSQL moves work into the application: joins, constraints, consistency
Many systems use both, each for what it does best
followUps: Tell me about a time the data model turned out to be wrong for the queries you needed.

questions.prompt: Your main table has outgrown a single database server. What do you try before sharding, and what changes once you shard?
questions.zh: 你们的主表已经大到单台数据库服务器撑不住了。分库分表之前你会先试什么？分了之后又会有哪些变化？
outline: First: optimize queries, add replicas, cache, archive old data, partition the table
Sharding costs: cross-shard queries, transactions, and operational complexity
Choose a shard key that spreads load and matches the main queries
Plan for resharding: consistent hashing, or a directory of logical shards
Consider a distributed SQL database before hand-rolling it
followUps: How do you generate unique IDs across shards?
How would you run a query that has to span every shard?

questions.prompt: How do you keep a cache and the database consistent, and what inconsistencies do you accept?
questions.zh: 你怎么保持缓存和数据库一致？哪些不一致是你可以接受的？
outline: Cache-aside: read the cache, on a miss load from the database and populate
On write: update the database first, then delete the cache key
Races can still leave stale data, so always set a TTL
Stronger options: a delayed second delete, or invalidating from the change log
Decide per data type how stale is acceptable

chunks.zh: 存活时间（缓存过期时间）

followUps: Why delete the cache entry instead of updating it in place?

questions.prompt: How do you change the schema of a large, busy table without downtime?
questions.zh: 一张数据量大、读写又很繁忙的表，你怎么在不停机的情况下改它的表结构？
outline: Expand and contract: add the new shape, migrate, then remove the old
Every step must work with both old and new application versions
Backfill in small throttled batches while watching replication lag
Know which changes lock the table; use online schema change tools
Verify the data before dropping anything; keep a way back
followUps: How would you rename a column that the running application still reads?

questions.prompt: You've added read replicas, and now users sometimes don't see their own changes. What's going on, and what do you do about it?
questions.zh: 你们加了只读副本之后，用户有时看不到自己刚做的修改。这是怎么回事？你怎么处理？
outline: Replication is asynchronous, so replicas lag behind the primary
Send a user's reads to the primary for a short time after they write
Or record the write position and wait until the replica has caught up
Monitor the lag and take badly lagging replicas out of rotation
Synchronous replication fixes it, at the cost of slower writes
followUps: What tends to cause replication lag to spike in the first place?

questions.prompt: Under load, your service starts timing out while waiting for a database connection. How do you investigate and fix it?
questions.zh: 一上负载，你的服务就在等待数据库连接时超时。你怎么排查和解决？
outline: The pool is exhausted: every connection is busy or has leaked
Look for slow queries, long transactions, and connections never returned
Do not make remote calls while holding a transaction open
Size the pool from what the database can handle; bigger is often worse
Total connections are pool size times instances; consider a connection proxy
followUps: Why can a larger connection pool make throughput worse?
